states.name: Apulia
timeline: Sparta's colony Taras on its great harbour; Iapygian peoples inland
Pythagoreans are recorded at Taras in Iamblichus' list of followers
Archippus, one of two survivors of the fire at Croton, settles at Taras

states.name: Basilicata
timeline: The Greek cities of Metapontum and Siris on the Gulf of Taranto
Pythagoras takes refuge at Metapontum
Pythagoras dies at Metapontum, by one account in the temple of the Muses (c. 495–490)
The revolts against the Pythagoreans spread to Metapontum (Polybius)

states.name: Calabria
timeline: Achaean and Locrian colonies: Croton, Sybaris, Locri, Rhegium; Oenotrian villages inland
Pythagoras arrives in Croton and addresses its elders, young men, boys and women
His followers, said to be three hundred, guide Croton's government
Croton destroys Sybaris; the army is led by the Pythagorean wrestler Milo
Cylon's faction attacks the brotherhood; Pythagoras leaves for Metapontum
The Pythagoreans recover their hold on Croton's politics
The house of Milo, the brotherhood's meeting place, is burned during a meeting (c. 450s)
Survivors regroup at Rhegium, at the toe of Italy

states.name: Campania
timeline: Greek Cumae and Poseidonia on the coast; Etruscan Capua inland
Refugees from Phocaea found Elea, later the city of Parmenides

states.name: Lazio
timeline: Latin towns and the kings of Rome; Etruscan cities to the north
By tradition, Rome expels its last king and becomes a republic

states.name: Toscana
timeline: The Etruscan cities at the height of their power

states.name: Sicily
timeline: Greek cities ring the coast: Syracuse, Akragas, Himera, Zankle; Sicels and Phoenicians
Refugees from Samos seize Zankle after the Ionian revolt
Greeks of Syracuse and Akragas defeat Carthage at Himera
At Akragas, Empedocles teaches the kinship of all living things

states.name: Sardegna
timeline: Nuragic peoples; Phoenician ports, soon under Carthage

states.name: Umbria
timeline: Umbrian hill towns and Etruscan Perusia and Volsinii

events.title: Born on Samos
events.text: Pythagoras, son of Mnesarchus, is born on the island of Samos, by Aristoxenus' reckoning about 570 BC.

events.title: Pherecydes of Syros
events.text: Later writers make Pythagoras a pupil of Pherecydes, an early prose writer on the gods.

events.title: Thales at Miletus
events.text: Iamblichus, eight centuries later, says the old Thales urged him to study in Egypt: a legend.

events.title: Phoenicia (legend)
events.text: Iamblichus has him study with the priests and sages of Sidon.

events.title: Egypt (legend)
events.text: Isocrates and Iamblichus send him to Egypt's temples; Iamblichus claims twenty-two years there.

events.title: Crete (legend)
events.text: Diogenes Laertius has him enter the cave of Mount Ida with the seer Epimenides.

events.title: Xenophanes goes west
events.text: The poet Xenophanes leaves Colophon; he will mock Pythagoras for hearing a friend's soul in a puppy.

events.title: Delphi (legend)
events.text: Aristoxenus says he learned his moral teaching from the Delphic priestess Themistoclea.

events.title: Elea founded
events.text: Refugees from Phocaea found Elea, later home of Parmenides.

events.title: Polycrates' tyranny
events.text: Polycrates seizes power on Samos and builds a fleet, temples and great works.

events.title: Eupalinos' tunnel
events.text: Samos cuts a kilometre-long water tunnel through a mountain from both ends, a feat of applied geometry.

events.title: Leaves Samos
events.text: At about forty, says Aristoxenus, Pythagoras leaves Samos to escape Polycrates' tyranny.

events.title: Arrival at Croton
events.text: Pythagoras reaches Croton, a rich Achaean colony in southern Italy, and speaks to its elders.

events.title: Garments for Hera
events.text: Iamblichus says the women of Croton, moved by his words, dedicated their costly clothes to Hera.

events.title: Egypt falls to Persia
events.text: Cambyses conquers Egypt; Iamblichus' story that Pythagoras was carried off to Babylon cannot fit his years in Croton.

events.title: Polycrates killed
events.text: The tyrant of Samos is lured to the mainland and killed by the Persian governor Oroetes.

events.title: The Three Hundred
events.text: His followers, bound by oath and said to number three hundred, come to guide Croton's council.

events.title: Milo at Olympia
events.text: Milo of Croton, a Pythagorean, wins the last of his six Olympic wrestling crowns around this time.

events.title: Sybaris destroyed
events.text: Croton's army, led by Milo, destroys its rich neighbour Sybaris.

events.title: Cylon's attack
events.text: Cylon, a rich Crotoniate refused admission, turns the city against the brotherhood (Aristoxenus).

events.title: Rome a republic
events.text: By Roman tradition, Rome expels its last king and becomes a republic.

events.title: Refuge at Metapontum
events.text: Pythagoras withdraws up the coast to Metapontum.

events.title: Alcmaeon of Croton
events.text: The physician Alcmaeon, later called a pupil of Pythagoras, studies the senses and the brain.

events.title: Heraclitus scoffs
events.text: At Ephesus, Heraclitus calls Pythagoras a collector of other men's learning.

events.title: Death at Metapontum
events.text: Pythagoras dies at Metapontum, by Dicaearchus' account after fasting in the temple of the Muses.

events.title: Miletus sacked
events.text: The Persians crush the Ionian revolt and destroy Miletus.

events.title: Samians at Zankle
events.text: Samians fleeing Persian rule sail west and seize Zankle in Sicily.

events.title: Hippasus (legend)
events.text: Iamblichus says Hippasus of Metapontum drowned at sea for revealing a secret of geometry.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: Syracuse and Akragas defeat a Carthaginian army in Sicily.

events.title: Parmenides at Elea
events.text: Parmenides, said to have learned from the Pythagorean Ameinias, writes his poem on being.

events.title: Philolaus
events.text: Philolaus is born at Croton or Taras; his book will set out the musical ratios in writing.

events.title: Empedocles
events.text: At Akragas, Empedocles teaches that souls pass between bodies and that all life is kin.

events.title: Milo's house burns
events.text: Enemies set fire to the meeting house at Croton during a gathering; nearly all inside die (c. 450s).

events.title: Revolts spread
events.text: Polybius says Pythagorean meeting houses were burned across Magna Graecia and the cities fell into turmoil.

events.title: Lysis to Thebes
events.text: Lysis, one of two survivors, flees to Thebes, where he later teaches the young Epaminondas.

events.title: Archippus to Taras
events.text: The other survivor, Archippus, goes home to Taras.

events.title: Regrouping at Rhegium
events.text: Aristoxenus says the remaining Pythagoreans gathered at Rhegium.

events.title: Achaean mediators
events.text: Polybius says the cities called on the Achaeans of Greece to settle the disputes.
